implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Specify needs
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This phase is triggered when a need for new statistics is identified, perhaps resulting from user feedback, or a review is undertaken. It includes all activities associated with engaging stakeholders to identify their detailed statistical needs (current or future), proposing high level solution options and preparing a business case, which may weigh the benefits of addressing these needs against expected costs, risks and other requirements, considering the public good arising from meeting those needs and the implications for respondents, users and other stakeholders. The Specify Needs phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 7), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This phase is triggered when a need for new statistics is identified, perhaps resulting from user feedback, or a review is undertaken. It includes all activities associated with engaging stakeholders to identify their detailed statistical needs (current or future), proposing high level solution options, and preparing a business case. In the modernized statistical environment, these activities are increasingly supported by automated and AI-powered processes—ranging from the synthesis and structuring of stakeholder inputs, through the analysis of options, to the automated drafting of business case materials. Routine and repetitive aspects of needs identification, consultation, and documentation are minimized for manual intervention, enabling staff to focus on higher-value tasks: interpreting context, establishing priorities, and making strategic decisions that cannot be automated. The phase thus leverages end-to-end process automation and AI wherever possible, supporting greater efficiency, responsiveness, and quality at the earliest stage of the statistical business process. The Specify Needs phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 7), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' role is affected by a shift to automation and AI-driven process automation in needs identification and documentation: 'Conducts data preparation techniques... ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' 'Supports the conduct of studies... using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods.' These analysts will now support digital/AI pipelines for needs analysis, validating outputs, and focusing on critical assessment, standardization, and deeper analysis instead of repetitive manual data gathering. The role's emphasis on 'data stewardship... to assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use' remains, but more of their day-to-day will involve interacting with, tuning, and critically appraising AI outputs.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Identify needs
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process includes the initial investigation and identification of what statistics are needed and what is needed of the statistics. It may be triggered by a new information request from users, an environmental change such as a reduced budget, a periodic review, or respondent feedback. Action plans from evaluations of previous iterations of the production cycle (including from respondent feedback) or from other programmes might provide an input to this sub-process. It also includes consideration of practice amongst other (national and international) statistical organisations producing similar data and the methods used by those organisations.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process includes the initial investigation and identification of what statistics are needed and what is needed of the statistics. In the modern process, AI and automated tools are used to continuously scan for new information requests from users, detect relevant environmental changes, and aggregate respondent feedback and evaluation action plans. These technologies also benchmark needs by automatically referencing practices among other (national and international) statistical organizations. Automation supports the collation, analysis, and structuring of these triggers for new or changed statistics, while staff focus their expertise on interpreting context, confirming significance, and ensuring response to complex or emergent requirements.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' conducts data preparation techniques and supports studies/projects involving statistical data analysis. They now partner with automation in gathering and classifying needs data, maintaining emphasis on 'ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' but shifting toward validation and review of AI-generated synthesized needs.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Check data availability and suitability
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process checks whether current sources of data could meet user requirements and the conditions under which they would be available, including any restrictions on their use. An assessment of possible alternatives would normally include research into potential administrative or other non-statistical sources of data (e.g. privately-held data or “Big Data”), to: Determine whether they would be suitable for use for statistical purposes (e.g. the extent to which administrative concepts match data requirements, and whether the timeliness and quality of the data, security, and continuity of data supply are suitable); Assess the division of responsibilities between data suppliers and the statistical organisation; Check necessary ICT resources (e.g. data storage, technology required to handle incoming data and data processing) as well as any provision agreements with data suppliers (which could be legal or other agreements such as memoranda of understanding) for accessing and sharing the data (e.g. formats, delivery, accompanying metadata and quality check). When existing sources have been assessed, a strategy for filling any remaining gaps in the data requirement is prepared. This may include identifying possible partnerships with data holders or conducting a new survey to collect data if necessary. This sub-process also includes a more general assessment of the legal framework in which data would be collected and used, and may therefore identify proposals for changes to existing legislation or the introduction of a new legal framework.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process systematically checks whether current sources of data could meet user requirements and the conditions under which they would be available, including any restrictions on their use. Existing data holdings must be exhaustively investigated and prioritized first, followed by a search for relevant administrative and alternative data sources; the option to conduct new surveys is only considered if these avenues prove insufficient to meet data needs. The subject matter sponsor holds sole accountability for certifying that all relevant avenues for data have been thoroughly explored and that the suitability, timeliness, and quality of any proposed source have been rigorously assessed. To expedite and strengthen the acquisition of administrative and alternative data, a center of expertise works collaboratively with subject matter specialists to support negotiations, acquisition logistics, and the establishment of legal or operational agreements where needed. When multiple avenues have been assessed and documented, a strategy for filling any remaining gaps is prepared. This sub-process also encompasses the assessment and possible updates to the legal framework for data collection, ensuring fit-for-purpose, respondent-efficient, and timely data acquisition and usage.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is implicated because the updated process requires staff who can 'validate AI/automation-enabled checks of data source quality, timeliness, and coverage,' and 'propose improvements and alternatives for data acquisition.' Their work-description specifies 'knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling...' and 'knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies...' Reinforcing a move to digital-first, automated sourcing, they will be required to focus on the technical assessment and validation of new (especially automated or alternative) data source quality and suitability.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Design
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This phase describes the development and design activities, and any associated practical research work needed to define the statistical outputs, variables, methodologies, collection instruments and operational processes, with due regard to other requirements such as security. It includes all the design elements needed to define or refine the statistical products or services identified in the business case. This phase specifies all relevant metadata, in accordance with the standards and corporate policies, ready for use later in the business process, as well as quality assurance procedures. For statistical outputs produced on a regular basis, this phase usually occurs for the first iteration and whenever improvement actions are identified in the Evaluate phase of a previous iteration. Design activities make substantial use of international and national standards in order to reduce the length and cost of the design process, and enhance interoperability, comparability, etc. Organisations may reuse or adapt design elements from existing processes and consider geospatial aspects of data in the design to enhance the usability and value of the statistical information. Additionally, outputs of design processes may form the basis for future standards at the organisational, national or international levels. The Design phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 8), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative. Some approaches used to develop tools and systems involve iteration between sub-processes in the Design and Build phases.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This phase describes the development and design activities, and any associated practical research work needed to define the statistical outputs, variables, methodologies, collection instruments, and operational processes—with a strong emphasis on automation, AI-powered tools, and digital interoperability. Automated and AI-driven processes play a central role in drafting specifications, aligning with corporate and international standards, generating and enriching metadata, simulating system interactions, and iterating design improvements. All statistical products and their supporting metadata are produced in standardized, richly described, and machine-actionable forms, ensuring they are interoperable and reusable across downstream tools, APIs, and organizational systems. Staff are freed from repetitive and routine design work and instead focus on innovation, calibration, and optimizing for evolving user and stakeholder requirements. Design activities thus promote efficiency, quality, and discoverability, embedding best practices for automation, standardization, and open data access. The Design phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 8), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, can occur in parallel, and may be iterative. Iteration between Design and Build phases is supported through automated versioning and process enhancements.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is required to have 'knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence...' and 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation.' With the Design phase now shifting to automation for specification, standards compliance, and output configuration, they shift toward validating, quality assuring, and contextualizing AI/automation-generated component and system designs.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Design variables
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process defines the variables to be collected via the collection instrument, as well as any other variables that will be derived from them in sub-process 5.5 (Derive new variables and units), and any statistical or geospatial classifications that will be used. This is also where unit types (including observation units and statistical units) can be designed. It is expected that existing national and international standards will be followed wherever possible. This sub-process may need to run in parallel with sub-process 2.3 (Design collection), as the definition of the variables to be collected and the choice of collection instruments may be inter-dependent to some degree. Preparation of metadata for collected and derived variables, statistical and geospatial classification is a necessary precondition for subsequent phases.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process defines the variables to be collected via the collection instrument and any that will be derived for analysis or dissemination, with a strong emphasis on standards compliance, automation, and machine-actionability. All variable definitions and supporting metadata must comply with national and international standards (e.g., SDMX), structured in machine-actionable formats and managed through prescribed data management tools (such as Aria or Colectica) to ensure robust lifecycle control and digital traceability. AI/LLM-enabled tools are used to generate, refine, and validate variable names, descriptions, and attributes, maximizing clarity, standardization, and discoverability. Staff involved in this sub-process are proficient in digital metadata standards and tooling, ensuring all variable-related products are interoperable, automation-ready, and reusable by both human and machine users. This ensures that the resulting statistical outputs are consistently described, easily found, and seamlessly integrated across digital platforms and systems.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is also implicated—'knowledge of data science and its life cycle... warehousing, cleansing, processing, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization' and 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation.' These skills adapt toward validation and enrichment of AI/LLM-derived variable sets, focusing on compliance and interoperability, and technical validation within modern metadata management systems.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Design collection
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process prepares a collection strategy for the data, and determines the most appropriate collection instruments and methods, which may depend on the type of data collection, the collection unit type (enterprise, person, or other) and the available sources of data. The actual activities in this sub-process will vary according to the type of collection instrument required, which can include computer assisted interviewing, paper questionnaires, administrative registers, automated and semi-automated data transfer methods (such as using APIs, machine-to-machine integrations and various types of file transfers), web-scraping technologies as well as technology for geospatial data. The collection may employ a multi-mode method which requires additional considerations such as design of sequencing or different instruments for different modes. Direct or indirect use of administrative data may be introduced in the data collection mode for either controlling survey data or assisting it when capturing survey information. In the case of survey (or census) data, this collection strategy includes the design of the collection instruments, questions and response templates (in conjunction with the variables and statistical classifications designed in sub-process 2.2 (Design variables)). It is important to understand respondents and incorporate the user perspectives in the design of data collection. This sub-process may include design of fieldwork operations, and respondent engagement, in the case of survey data collection. It also includes the confirmation of existing agreements or creation of new agreements. This sub-process is enabled by tools such as question libraries (to facilitate the reuse of questions and related attributes), questionnaire tools (to enable the quick and easy compilation of questions into formats suitable for cognitive testing) and agreement templates (to help standardise terms and conditions). This sub-process also includes the design of respondent management systems that are specific to this business process. Where statistical organisations do not collect data directly (i.e. a third party controls the collection and processing of the data), this sub-process may include the design of mechanisms to monitor the data and the metadata to assess impacts of any change made by the third party.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process prepares a collection strategy for the data and determines the most appropriate collection instruments and methods, with a strategic emphasis on automation, AI/ML, and passive acquisition. Where possible, the design must prioritize passive, administrative, and already-available sources of data; surveys or direct solicitation are employed only when all other avenues are exhausted or cannot provide suitable data. All aspects of collection design—including the configuration of instruments, sequencing, respondent communications, and integration agreements—should embed automation, machine-to-machine interfaces, digital event/trigger-based collection, and minimal manual intervention. Where a survey instrument is essential, automated and AI-driven methods must be used for design, rendering, and fielding, ensuring quick turnaround, reduced burden, and full standards compliance. The sub-process also entails the necessary design of respondent management, monitoring, and adaptive feedback loops to maximize efficiency and data quality, while reserving human staff for exception handling and final validation.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is also involved, with skills in 'data capture and acquisition, data extraction... processing...' and 'knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies...' Their work will now emphasize vetting, QA, and technical support for automated, digital-first collection system designs (including passive acquisition, APIs, AI-driven survey logic/design).

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Design frame and sample
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process applies especially to processes which involve data collection based on sampling, such as through statistical surveys, but it may also apply to other types of data collection such as census or register-based (e.g., filtering of registers based on the target population). It identifies and specifies the population of interest, defines a sampling frame (and, where necessary, the register from which it is derived), and determines the most appropriate sampling criteria and methodology (which could include complete enumeration). Common sources for a sampling frame are administrative and statistical registers, censuses and information from other sample surveys. It may refer to geospatial data and classifications. This sub-process describes how these sources can be combined if needed. Analysis of whether the frame covers the target population should be performed. Spatial analysis techniques can be used to ensure the spatial distribution of the units is appropriate. A sampling plan should be made. The actual sample is created in sub-process 4.1 (Create frame and select sample), using the methodology specified in this sub-process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process, which applies to all statistical processes involving sampling, is built around digital automation, flexibility, and data quality by design. Whenever frames or registers from administrative, alternative, or partner-held sources are used, partners are expected and supported to apply AI-driven data cleaning and quality control processes prior to data ingestion by Statistics Canada—improving coverage, comparability, and downstream analytic value. The specification of the population of interest, development of the sampling frame, and establishment of sampling criteria and methodology are designed for full integration with end-to-end digital pipelines, supporting automated and seamless flow between pre-collection and post-collection business processes, drastically reducing manual involvement and risk of programmatic 'patches.' Sampling designs must explicitly allow for a range of dynamic and flexible options (including person-based and adaptive sampling), with supporting digital tools enabling real-time optimization informed by diverse data realities and program goals. This ensures the most efficient, quality-driven, and responsive sampling methodologies possible.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is implicated, as they are familiar with 'data preparation techniques..., data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' and participate 'in project teams and working groups to support data management, research and analysis, and other unit activities.' Their technical role expands into the QA and supervision of AI-enabled and partner-prepared frames, oversight for integration into digital workflows, and adoption/support of flexible sampling designs.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Design processing and analysis
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process designs the statistical methodology to be applied during the Process and Analyse phases. This can include, among others, specification of routines and rules for coding, editing and imputation, which may vary based on the means of data collection and source of data. This subprocess also includes design of specifications for data integration from multiple data sources, validation of data and estimation. Statistical disclosure control methods are also designed here if they are specific to this business process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process designs the statistical methodology to be applied during the Process and Analyse phases, with a core emphasis on standards-based automation, AI enablement, and digital interoperability. Specifications for routines and rules covering coding, editing, imputation, validation, and data integration/estimation are required to be implemented, where practical, using automated frameworks and AI/ML-driven tools—leveraging SDMX models, .STAT processing, and corporate-standard solutions (e.g., Aria/Colectica). Human analysts and methodologists are focused on reviewing and updating analytic methods for non-standard or novel use-cases, with all standardizable and repeatable components digital, automated, and reproducible by default. Statistical disclosure control and quality assurance methods designed here also leverage automation and AI for rapid, secure, and scalable deployment. All methodologies are documented to be compatible with downstream digital workflows and to support auditing, versioning, and continuous improvement.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst'—with 'knowledge of data science..., data cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting...'—will now focus on implementing, reviewing, documenting, and testing automated/AI-driven analytical routines and ensuring complete digital traceability and standards compliance.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Design production systems and workflows
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process determines the workflow from data collection to dissemination, taking an overview of all the processes required within the whole production process and ensuring that they fit together efficiently with no gaps or redundancies. Various systems and databases may be needed throughout the process. The GSBPM can be used to design a statistical organisation’s business architecture layer when a statistical organisation has an existing enterprise architecture in place. The design might be adjusted to fit the organisation. A general principle is to reuse processes and technology across many statistical business processes, so existing production solutions (e.g. services, systems and databases) should be examined first, to determine whether they are fit for purpose for this specific production process, then, if any gaps are identified, new solutions can be designed. This sub-process also considers how staff will interact with systems and who will be responsible for what and when.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process determines the workflow from data collection to dissemination, ensuring all production processes are seamlessly integrated, modular, and event-driven, with automation and AI/ML supporting orchestration, monitoring, and transitions. Workflows are designed to minimize manual intervention and maximize real-time coordination, leveraging digital platforms and automation for every routine or standardized task. The emphasis is on building touchless, continuous data pipelines that allow for automated validation, routing, escalation, and exception reporting. Existing automated solutions and system components are reused wherever possible; if new components are needed, they are built automation- and integration-ready from inception. Staff responsibilities focus on system oversight, addressing exceptions and inefficiencies, and iteratively improving and upgrading automated workflows for future resilience and scalability.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is expected to support and validate 'modular, automation-ready, and event-driven digital pipelines,' ensuring end-to-end system integrity and smooth transitions between all process phases. Their technical skills, knowledge of workflow configuration, and partnership on 'project teams and working groups to support data management, research and analysis' will now be directed toward the implementation and refinement of digital-first, inter-operable workflows across the statistic production lifecycle.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Build
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This phase builds and tests the production solution to the point where it is ready for use in the 'live' environment. The outputs of the Design phase are assembled and configured in this phase to create the complete operational environment to run the process. New services are built by exception, created in response to gaps in the existing catalogue of services sourced from within the organisation and externally. These new services are constructed to be broadly reusable in alignment with the business architecture of the organisation where possible, and compliant with security requirements. For statistical outputs produced on a regular basis, this phase usually occurs for the first iteration, following a review or a change in methodology or technology, rather than for every iteration. The Build phase is broken down into seven sub-processes (Figure 9), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative. Some approaches used to develop tools and systems involve iteration between sub-processes in the Design and Build phases. The first three sub-processes are concerned with the development and improvement of systems used in collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of data. The last four subprocesses focus on the end-to-end process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This phase builds and tests the production solution to the point where it is ready for use in the 'live' environment, leveraging modular automation and AI-driven assembly at every step. The outputs of the Design phase are assembled and configured using digital orchestration pipelines that prioritize reusability, traceability, and compliance with business architecture and security requirements. Automated configuration, integration, and self-testing are employed wherever possible, enabling rapid, reliable, and consistent system deployment. Human expertise is reserved for overseeing automated processes, handling exceptions that cannot be resolved by automation, and driving continuous improvement in modular service creation. New services are developed only to fill gaps, and are built from inception for automation compatibility, modularity, and compliance. The Build phase is structured into seven sub-processes (Figure 9), supporting iteration and parallelization, and is tightly integrated with Design to ensure seamless translation of specifications into robust operational environments.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is also implicated, due to their technical activities with 'data preparation techniques,' system configuration, 'data validation,' and support of studies/projects involving data analysis and processing. As automation is prioritized for assembling and configuring production environments, their work will focus on QA, troubleshooting exceptions, and overseeing the real-time integration and deployment of automated components and data flows.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process describes the activities to reuse existing components or build new components needed for the Process and Analyse phases, as designed in the Design phase. Services (re-)used may include dashboard functions and features, information services, transformation functions, geospatial data services, workflow management tools, respondent and metadata management services.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process describes the activities to reuse existing components or build new, automation-ready components needed for the Process and Analyse phases. All components—whether dashboard modules, transformation functions, geospatial and information services, or workflow management tools—must be designed for modularity, AI/ML-driven orchestration, and seamless integration into digital, event-driven workflows. Automated self-testing, monitoring, and dynamic integration APIs are core features, enabling real-time responsiveness and automated exchange of data and instructions. Human roles focus on oversight, quality assurance, exception management, and iterative modernization of core analytic assets. The process ensures that the full analytics and processing stack evolves toward touchless, scalable, and intelligent operational pipelines.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: GSBPM updates require all components to be 'built or retrofitted for automation, event-driven orchestration, and plug-and-play integration.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' is responsible for supporting 'data preparation techniques,' 'organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies,' and participates in teams for 'data management, research and analysis.' They will need to validate, configure, and ensure technical interoperability of AI/automation-ready analytical and processing modules, testing outputs and troubleshooting integration issues.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Configure workflows
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process configures the workflows, systems and transformations used within the business processes, from data collection through to dissemination. In this sub-process, the workflows are configured based on the design created in sub-process 2.6 (Design production systems and workflows). This could include modifying a standardised workflow for a specific purpose, assembling the workflows for the different phases together (possibly with a workflow/business process management system) and configuring systems accordingly.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process configures the workflows, systems, and transformations used within all business processes—from data collection through to dissemination—to form modular, automation-ready data pipelines. Workflows are assembled, customized, and deployed using digital workflow or business process management platforms, with extensive AI/automation support for orchestration, process monitoring, and autonomous task triggering. These workflows enable seamless, hands-free movement of data and outputs between business process stages, allowing real-time responsiveness and minimizing the need for manual intervention. Human involvement is limited to oversight, rapid workflow adaptation where unique business needs arise, and exception escalation that cannot be managed automatically.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' also plays a part by testing, validating, and advising on digital workflow configuration to support seamless transitions throughout the statistical pipeline. Their technical familiarity with data and process management translates into assisting pipeline monitoring, identifying inefficiencies, and ensuring workflows are correctly parameterized for automation and rapid response.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Create frame and select sample
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process establishes the frame and selects the sample for this iteration of the collection, as specified in sub-process 2.4 (Design frame and sample). It also includes the coordination of samples between instances of the same business process (e.g. to manage overlap or rotation), and between different processes using a common frame or register (e.g. to manage overlap or to spread response burden). Quality assurance and approval of the frame and the selected sample are also undertaken in this sub-process, though maintenance of underlying registers, from which frames for several statistical business processes are drawn, is treated as a separate activity. The sampling aspect of this sub-process is often not relevant for processes based entirely on the use of preexisting sources (e.g. administrative sources and other non-survey sources) as such processes generally create frames from the available data and then follow a census approach. Variables from administrative and other non-statistical sources of data can be used as auxiliary variables in the construction of sampling design.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process establishes the frame and selects the sample for this iteration of the collection, as specified in sub-process 2.4 (Design frame and sample). Automated and AI/LLM-driven technologies are employed to perform record linkage, deduplication, and harmonization across administrative, alternative, and legacy data sources, ensuring the sampling frame is accurate, comprehensive, and consistent. These tools facilitate quality assurance and enhance sample design, especially when coordinating samples between concurrent or overlapping statistical processes. Human experts review, refine, and sign off on the final sampling frame and sample selection, focusing attention on resolving any exceptions or ambiguities surfaced by automated systems.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The GSBPM update requires use of AI/LLM tools for 'record linkage, deduplication, and harmonization across administrative, alternative, and legacy data sources,' improving frame quality. The 'Junior Data Analyst'—with responsibilities for 'data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin'—will primarily validate, QA, and interpret automated frame construction outputs. They will address edge cases, support harmonization efforts, and oversee the integrity of sampling frames generated or enhanced by automation.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Process
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This phase describes the processing of input data and their preparation for analysis. It is made up of sub-processes that integrate, classify, check, clean, and transform input data, so that they can be analysed and disseminated as statistical outputs. For statistical outputs produced regularly, this phase occurs in each iteration. The sub-processes in this phase can apply to data from both statistical and non-statistical sources (with the possible exception of sub-process 5.6 (Calculate weights), which is usually specific to survey data). Some variables could be processed prior to others if they are required for data integration (e.g., geospatial variables if used for that purpose). The Process and Analyse phases can be iterative and parallel. Analysis can reveal a broader understanding of the data, which might make it apparent that additional processing is needed. Sometimes the estimates being processed might be already published aggregates (undertaken according to a Revision Policy). Activities within the Process and Analyse phases may also commence before the Collect phase is completed. This enables the compilation of provisional results where timeliness is an important concern for users, and increases the time available for analysis. The Process phase is broken down into eight sub-processes (Figure 11), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This phase describes the processing of input data and their preparation for analysis, using modular, version-controlled, automation- and AI/ML-enabled digital workflows. Every sub-process—integrate, classify, check, clean, and transform input data—is configured for event-driven orchestration, reproducibility, and end-to-end automation wherever feasible, ensuring high speed, quality, and consistency. Routine manipulation, error-checking, cleaning, imputation, and integration are handled by AI-enabled modules, with 50% or more of manual interventions eliminated. All processing operations produce full audit trails and documentation for traceability, enabling rapid adjustment and continuous process improvement. Analysts and staff focus on process oversight, exception handling, and innovation, while ensuring all processed outputs are standardized, metadata-rich, and downstream-ready for analysis and dissemination. The Process phase is broken down into eight sub-processes (Figure 11), which may run sequentially, in parallel, or iteratively, as determined by automated orchestration and analytic requirements.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The GSBPM update requires all processing activities—integrating, classifying, transforming, checking, cleaning—to be 'handled via modular, version-controlled, automation-ready digital pipelines, with AI/ML enabling scalable, event-driven, and reproducible execution for each sub-process.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' (‘conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin’) will need to shift from manual execution to oversight, QA, and process innovation for AI/automation-driven pipelines. They focus on configuration, review of exception reports, and iterative improvement of automated processing.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Integrate data
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process integrates data from one or more sources. It is where the results of subprocesses in the Collect phase are combined. The input data can be from a mixture of external or internal sources, and a variety of collection instruments, including extracts of administrative and other non-statistical data sources. Administrative data or other non-statistical sources of data can substitute for all or some of the variables directly collected from a survey. This sub-process also includes harmonising or creating new figures that agree between sources of data. The result is a consolidated set of data.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process integrates data from one or more sources using automated, modular, and AI/LLM-powered pipelines. Record linkage, deduplication, and harmonization are conducted with machine learning and automation as the core methods, minimizing manual intervention. Integration pipelines are event-driven, version-controlled, and produce full audit trails for traceability and continuous improvement. Human experts intervene only to review targeted anomalies, exceptions, and complex analytic challenges, ensuring the integrated dataset is accurate, comprehensive, and ready for further analysis.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The update calls for 'automated, AI/LLM-powered routines for record linking, harmonization, and consolidation of disparate datasets.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' is already experienced in 'data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation.' Now, they supervise, validate, and QA the automated integration outputs, perform expert review of flagged discrepancies or exceptions, and optimize pipelines to achieve reliable consolidated datasets.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Classify and code
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process classifies and codes the input data. For example, automatic (or clerical) coding routines may assign numeric codes to text responses according to a pre-determined statistical classification to facilitate data capture and processing. Some questions have coded response categories on the questionnaires or administrative source of data, others are coded after collection using an automated process (which may apply machine learning or artificial intelligence techniques) or an interactive, manual process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process classifies and codes input data using modular, automated, and AI/ML-powered pipelines that leverage SDMX and other international standards. Text descriptions and response data are classified and coded primarily by LLM/AI models, which assign pre-determined statistical, geospatial, or industry codes with minimal manual handling. The workflow is event-driven, digitally logged, subject to automated QA/review, and fully auditable. Manual intervention is reserved for new or ambiguous cases, or as last-resort exception handling with domain-expert validation. This approach maximizes accuracy, speed, traceability, and scalability for coding/classification at all process scales.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Standardization (e.g., SDMX), event-driven AI/automation, and LLM-powered classification/coding (e.g., NAICS codes) become the default. The 'Junior Data Analyst' role—whose duties include 'data preparation,' 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation'—now requires skills for configuring, validating, and troubleshooting automated classification/coding flows, reviewing outputs, and escalating ambiguous cases for further judgment.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Review and validate
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process examines data to identify potential problems, errors and discrepancies such as outliers, item non-response, miscoding and duplicate records. It can also be referred to as input data validation. It may be run iteratively, validating data against pre-defined edit rules, usually in a set order. It may flag data for automatic or manual inspection or editing. Reviewing and validating can apply to data from any type of source, before and after integration, as well as imputed data from sub-process 5.4 (Edit and impute). Whilst validation is treated as part of the Process phase, in practice, some elements of validation may occur alongside collection activities, particularly for approaches such as computer assisted collection. Whilst this sub-process is concerned with detection and localisation of actual or potential errors, any correction activities that actually change the data is done in sub-process 5.4 (Edit and impute).
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process examines and validates data using modular, automated digital tools and AI/LLM-enabled validation routines. ML and LLMs flag missing data, inconsistencies, outliers, and errors, routing only ambiguous, complex, or systemic anomalies to human experts for further investigation and correction. All validation is digitally orchestrated with complete audit logging, reproducibility, and ongoing version control. This approach ensures rapid, scalable, and transparent validation with minimal manual intervention, allowing for continuous adjustment and quality improvement.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Routine validation and error/outlier/anomaly detection is automated (AI/LLM), while complex or ambiguous cases go to humans. The 'Junior Data Analyst', tasked with 'ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards...,' will now concentrate on reviewing automated validation reports, responding to escalations from digital pipelines, and suggesting edits or QA rule improvements to continually sharpen automated routines.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Edit and impute
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: Where data are considered incorrect, missing, unreliable, outdated, or duplicated, new values may be inserted, or erroneous data may be removed in this sub-process. The terms editing and imputation cover a variety of methods to do this, often using a rule-based approach. Specific steps typically include: Determining whether to add or change data; Selecting the method to be used; Adding/changing data values; Writing the new data values back to the data set, and flagging them as changed; Producing metadata on the editing and imputation process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: Where data are considered incorrect, missing, unreliable, outdated, or duplicated, edits and imputations are made through automated, modular, and AI/LLM-powered digital pipelines. LLMs and ML modules suggest and apply replacements or corrections as standard, tracking all actions and metadata in a comprehensive audit trail. Human analysts intervene only for novel, complex, or systemic data problems, and for reviewing and signing off automated edits where required. This ensures fast, accurate, and transparent correction of data with minimal manual processing.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: AI/LLM-driven imputation and edit routines are now standard. The 'Junior Data Analyst'—responsible for data cleansing and transformation—reviews AI-suggested edits, ensures proper logging, investigates cases not resolved by automation, and audits the integrity of metadata on the edit/impute process.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Derive new variables and units
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process derives data for variables and units that are not explicitly provided in the collection, but are needed to deliver the required outputs. It derives new variables by applying arithmetic formulae to one or more of the variables that are already present in the dataset, or applying different model assumptions. This activity may need to be iterative, as some derived variables may themselves be based on other derived variables. It is therefore important to ensure that variables are derived in the correct order. New units may be derived by aggregating or splitting data for collection units, or by various other estimation methods. Examples include deriving households where the collection units are persons or enterprises where the collection units are legal units.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process derives data for variables and units needed to deliver required outputs using modular, automation- and AI-powered methods. Digital pipelines apply arithmetic and formula-based logic, iterating as needed and recording all derivations and transformations with a traceable audit trail. Manual intervention is reserved for rare, non-standard or complex derivations beyond automation, with staff focusing on validation and insight for exceptions. This structure maximizes efficiency, reproducibility, and transparency in all variable/unit derivation steps.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Variable/unit derivations are now 'modular, automation-ready, and AI-powered.' The 'Junior Data Analyst'—with skills in 'modeling, summarization, reporting'—focuses on validating, reviewing, and fine-tuning AI-derived new variables, as well as checking the audit trail and ensuring all derivations conform to expected logic and implementation.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Calculate weights
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process creates weights for unit data records according to the methodology developed in sub-process 2.5 (Design processing and analysis). For example, weights can be used to 'gross-up' data to make them representative of the target population (e.g. for sample surveys or extracts of scanner data), or to adjust for non-response in total enumerations. In other situations, variables may need weighting for normalisation purposes. It may also include weight correction for benchmarking indicators (e.g. known population totals).
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process creates weights for unit data records through modular, event-driven automated algorithms, according to methodologies determined in phase 2.5. All steps and formulae, including adjustments for non-response or benchmarking, are handled digitally and recorded in procedural audit logs. Staff intervene when innovative methods, unexpected results, or diagnostic reviews are needed; otherwise, the process runs hands-free, ensuring speed, precision, and traceability in weight calculation.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Weight calculation is now performed by 'modular, event-driven automated algorithms,' with staff role limited to review of diagnostics, exceptions and innovative methods. The 'Junior Data Analyst' will QA weights, manage exceptions, and validate automated chain logs against established methodology and expected results.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Calculate aggregates
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process creates aggregate data and population totals from microdata or lower-level aggregates. It includes summing data for records sharing certain characteristics (e.g. aggregation of data by demographic or geographic classifications), determining measures of average and dispersion, and applying weights from sub-process 5.6 (Calculate weights) to derive appropriate totals. In the case of statistical outputs which use sample surveys, sampling errors corresponding to relevant aggregates may also be calculated in this sub-process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process creates aggregate data and population totals using modular, digital automation pipelines, generating all statistical summaries, weights, and dispersion measures hands-free. Event-driven algorithms apply the full range of aggregations, error calculations, and summary statistic logic, recording all processes in comprehensive audit logs for traceability and QA. Human expert action is required only for advanced analytic extensions or for reviewing flagged anomalies or exceptions in automated results.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Aggregations, summary statistics, and error calculations are conducted in 'modular, automated pipelines.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' ensures the reproducibility and integrity of aggregation outputs, reviews audit trails, and supervises exceptions or advanced analyses beyond automated scope.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Finalise data files
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process brings together the results of the other sub-processes in this phase in a data set (either micro- or macro-data), which is used as the input to the Analyse phase. Sometimes, this may be an intermediate rather than a final data set, particularly for business processes where there are strong time pressures, and a requirement to produce both preliminary and final estimates.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process brings together and finalizes the results of all previous sub-processes in the phase, producing data files (micro- or macro-level) in fully standardized, open, and machine-actionable formats by default. All datasets and supporting documentation are versioned, digitally logged, and immediately available for reproducible handoff to subsequent analysis or dissemination phases. Technical staff ensure compliance with standards and continuous skills development, and all processes are supported by automated documentation and audit trails, supporting immediate traceability, interoperability, and readiness for deployment across business domains.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' must support documentation and QA of new automated outputs, enforce standards, validate technical hand-off, and conduct audits or troubleshooting where needed. Their role requires technical proficiency and validation mindset to guarantee all outputs meet evolving standards for machine/human consumption.
